answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a bonding-fee spiral: each new identity posts a refundable bond it gets back only after completing peer-verified honest work. The bond spirals upward with every identity spawned from the same funding wallet, so a single operator minting thousands of fakes faces compounding costs, each sybil more expensive than the last. Honest agents reclaim their stake like nectar drawn back to the hive, abandoned fakes forfeit theirs into a commons fund, and the worthless ones drift off on a zephyr.
